subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should every CLI, RPC, and queued operator cron run record its outcome but never consume one-shots or mutate scheduler counters, alerts, backoff, next-run timing, or enabled state?
rationale: The linked bug establishes that manual runs must not destroy scheduled one-shots, but making all operator outcomes fully observational is a broader durable product contract that automation should not choose.

options.title: Adopt observational operator runs
options.body: Approve the explicit-origin model so only timer and watcher-terminal executions own scheduler state.

options.title: Narrow the fix
options.body: Preserve deleteAfterRun jobs while defining which manual outcomes may still affect alerts, counters, or retry state.

options.title: Pause for cron policy
options.body: Keep the branch open until the manual-versus-scheduled ownership contract is resolved with the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Adopt observational operator runs
recommendation.body: Approve the explicit-origin model so only timer and watcher-terminal executions own scheduler state.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent cron operation history makes this the best available routing candidate for the permanent public behavior decision.
